correctness.rationale: Setting both inputs to zero gives Rp=0. Setting v=0 gives R[u,p]=[Ru,p]; with u=0, antisymmetry and the first relation give R²v=Rv. After these terms cancel, the bilinear identity for u=a+b and v=c+d is R([a,c]−[b,d])=[a,c]. It holds exactly for complementary Lie subalgebras A and B, with p∈B normalizing A. The bracket-preserving affine group has precisely a Lie automorphism as linear part and a central shift: evaluating bracket preservation with an input zero forces the shift central. Its action on p adds (I−R') times the central shift to the image of p. All lines are subalgebras, and a plane is one exactly when it contains the center, since independent quotient directions bracket to a nonzero central vector. An adapted pair of lifts and its bracket conjugate each ordered decomposed pair to the displayed representative pair. In rank one, the normalizer condition forces the translation central, so it can be removed; in rank two the center is in the image, so the central shifts cannot change p, and stabilizer rescaling gives exactly the zero and nonzero classes. Constants split by centrality, and rank three forces the identity. Over F_q there are q+1 central planes and q² complementary lines per plane. Multiplying by the permitted shifts gives q³(q+1) in rank one and q²(q+1), q²(q²−1) in rank two; the constant orbits and identity give q³(2q+3)+1 in total. The reasoning uses field linear algebra, not residue arithmetic, so covers nonprime odd q. The bundled code and notes were inspected but not executed; the finite checks build candidates and do not independently establish their completeness.

value.rationale: This is a complete normal-form classification for a natural first nonabelian nilpotent test case beyond dimension two. It exhibits a structural distinction missed by a linear census: a rank-one allowed shift can be conjugated away, whereas rank two retains a nonzero-shift orbit. Exact orbit sizes over arbitrary odd finite fields quantify that distinction and are useful for distinguishing affine from linear classifications.
